newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 27.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik proposes that the limit for required registration for value added tax (DPH) payers increase from a current 750,000 crowns to a 500,000 crowns turn-over for three consecutive months. The new proposal will be taken up by the cabinet soon.

- Russia has promised that it will begin to pay off its debt to the Czech Republic which amounts to 3.4 billion dollars. Yearly payments of approximately 5.13 billion crowns will be made, from which $126 million will be counted as interest.

- According to a court ruling which was approved by the cabinet at the end of last year, if domestic and foreign companies are interested in importing and exporting materials with Czech components to and from the Czech Republic on the basis of a preferential regime, the imported components must come from CEFTA, EFTA or the European Union.

PRAVO - Member of parliament and chairman of the budget committee, Jozef Wagner was for the second time in six weeks expelled from the Social Democratic Party (CSSD). The central executive committee (UVV) of CSSD discharged his membership on Sunday.

- Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, after returning from his visit to Moscow last week, expressed his dissatisfaction with the fact that even during the third meeting of the Intercabinet Commission there was no progress made towards finding an answer to the question concerning the transport of natural gas from Kazakhstan through Russia to the Czech Republic.

- Belgian Kredietbank, a relatively high ranking world bank, on Friday officially announced that it will participate in substantially increasing the basic assets of Banka Hana (BH). On Thursday, shareholders of BH approved an increase in capital of 0.9 to 1.2 billion crowns to 2.7 to 3 billion crowns.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - General Faculty Hospital in Prague owes its distributors, including its distributors of medicine, approximately 0.75 billion crowns, and due to a lack of funds does not have enough medicine to meet demands. In the past few days, many pacients have not received the medicines they require.

- During the March conference of the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), the party will have to find a new chairman. The current chairman, Jan Kalvoda, who resigned as representative and minister after the affair of his false title of doctor of law, announced on Saturday that he will no longer be a candidate for any post in ODA.
